desc:
Encoding. A singly linked structure with n nodes is given as a successor array. The nodes are numbered 0..n-1 and succ[i] is the number of the node that follows node i, or -1 if node i has no next node. The list starts at node 0 (its head).

Starting at the head and repeatedly following succ, the walk either reaches a node with succ = -1 (the list ends) or never stops because it re-enters a node it has already visited (the list has a cycle). Return true if the list that starts at node 0 has a cycle and false otherwise.

Nodes that cannot be reached from node 0 are not part of the list, so a loop among them does not count. For succ = [1,2,3,1] the walk is 0, 1, 2, 3, 1, ... and the answer is true; for succ = [1,-1,2] the list is 0 -> 1, node 2 points to itself but is unreachable, so the answer is false.

Try to use O(1) extra memory.
constraints: Some nodes may be unreachable from node 0; they are ignored
hints: Storing every visited node in a set and stopping when you see a repeat works, but needs O(n) memory.
Imagine two runners on the list: one moves one node per turn, the other two nodes per turn. What happens to the fast one if the list ends? What if it loops?
Move slow by one node and fast by two. If fast (or the node after it) is -1, there is no cycle. If slow == fast at some turn, there is one.
editorial: Use Floyd's tortoise and hare. Both pointers start at the head; each turn slow advances by one node and fast by two. In an acyclic list the fast pointer reaches -1 after about n/2 turns and the loop ends with false.

If the list contains a cycle, both pointers eventually enter it. From then on the distance between them inside the cycle shrinks by exactly one per turn (the fast one gains one node on the slow one), so it hits zero before the slow pointer has completed a full lap, and they meet. That gives true.

Only nodes reachable from node 0 are ever touched, so a loop among unreachable decoy nodes is never seen. The running time is O(n) and only two pointers are stored, so the space is O(1). The set based version has the same time but O(n) space.
